claims.text: HEBM followed by SPS can suppress porosity in CoCrFeNiTi.
The proposed process will produce 100–500 nm grains in CoCrFeNiTi.
The resulting CoCrFeNiTi structure will be FCC-dominated with a minor BCC fraction and suppressed HCP formation.
HEBM in argon at 300–400 rpm for 10–20 h followed by SPS at 900–1050 °C, 30–50 MPa, and 5–10 min is a suitable processing regime.
Heating rates of 50–100 °C/min and a short dwell provide the relevant strain-rate control during sintering.
The SPS displacement rate is limited by applying a pressure of 30–50 MPa.
The 900–1050 °C regime is above the recrystallization temperature of the FCC matrix while remaining below the melting point associated with Ti-rich HCP material.
HEBM introduces dislocations and defects that lower the activation energy for solid-solution formation and promote amorphization.
Rapid SPS supplies enough diffusion for nanocrystalline grain development but is too brief for substantial HCP nucleation and growth.
The HCP phase has a higher nucleation barrier than the competing phases in this CoCrFeNiTi composition.
High configurational entropy and kinetic trapping stabilize the FCC solid solution.
Local Ti enrichment produces a dispersed minor BCC phase.
An SPS pressure of 30–50 MPa ensures near-full densification and eliminates porosity.
Nb addition to CoCrFeNi led to Laves-phase formation in node::W4387048519.
The processed alloy will attain greater than 98% relative density.
The processed alloy will reach 450–650 HV, compared with approximately 200 HV for the cast state.
The processed alloy will have tensile strength of 800–1000 MPa and elongation greater than 20%.
The microstructure will contain 80–90 vol% FCC, 10–20 vol% BCC, and less than 5 vol% HCP.
Ti contents above 25 at% or sintering temperatures above 1100 °C are expected to promote HCP formation, while the strategy remains valid up to about 20 at% Ti.
A Vickers test at 500 g for 15 s is an established test condition for a mechanically alloyed and SPS-processed CoCrFeNi-based HEA.
